title: Canary upgrade with rollback
description: Upgrades roll out to a small canary slice first while metrics are watched: error rate, latency, and business signals. If the canary degrades beyond thresholds, the upgrade rolls back automatically. Only a healthy canary proceeds to full rollout. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers upgrading a small canary slice first.

LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: {"err": 0.01}, 2: {"err": 0.04}, 3: {"err": 0.12}}
err = CFG[LEVEL]["err"]
THRESHOLD = 0.05
print("canary error rate: %.2f%%" % (err * 100), "->", "ROLL BACK" if err > THRESHOLD else "proceed to full rollout")

title: Deprecation schedule tracker
description: Deprecated versions carry a removal date, and the tracker warns owners as the date approaches: 90 days, 30 days, 7 days. After removal, the old version is blocked. Schedules give consumers time to migrate without surprise breakage. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers tracking removal dates per deprecated version.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 120, 2: 20, 3: 3}
days_left = CFG[LEVEL]
if days_left > 90: status = "ok"
elif days_left > 30: status = "warning: 90-day notice passed"
elif days_left > 7: status = "urgent: 30-day notice passed"
elif days_left > 0: status = "CRITICAL: removal in %d days" % days_left
else: status = "BLOCKED: version removed"
print("days to removal:", days_left, "->", status)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: ABI/API break detector
description: The detector compares the public interface of two versions: removed functions, changed signatures, and altered behavior flags. Breaking changes are listed explicitly so upgrade reviewers know exactly what to fix. Non-breaking additions pass silently. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers diffing public interfaces between versions.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: ({"f": ["x"], "g": ["x", "y"]}, {"f": ["x"], "g": ["x", "y"], "h": ["z"]}), 2: ({"f": ["x"], "g": ["x", "y"]}, {"f": ["x"], "g": ["x"]}), 3: ({"f": ["x"]}, {"g": ["x"]})}
old, new = CFG[LEVEL]
breaks = [fn for fn in old if fn not in new or old[fn] != new[fn]]
added = [fn for fn in new if fn not in old]
print("breaking:", breaks or ["none"], "| added (safe):", added or ["none"])
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.
